variables.name: MAX_IN_FLIGHT
variables.help: Max number of concurrent fetches to deduplicate. Older entries are evicted when exceeded

variables.name: FILE_HOST_BIND
variables.help:
Address to listen on.

`FILE_HOST_BIND`, not `HOST`: zsh exports `HOST` as the machine's name. These two were once `HOST`/`PORT` and read by nothing (the listener was hard-coded to `0.0.0.0:3000`); the defaults are that address, so honouring them changes nothing for a server started without them.

variables.name: FILE_HOST_PORT
variables.help:
Port to listen on.

`FILE_HOST_PORT`, not `PORT`: the container reads the repo's `.env`, and a bare `PORT` there meant for another service would move this one.

variables.name: FILE_HOST_PORT_FALLBACK
variables.help: Dev only: when the port is taken, listen on the next free one instead of failing (`listen::bind`). `make dev` sets it, so a server run from source can sit beside the production container. Never set it in production: its published port and healthcheck assume `FILE_HOST_PORT`

variables.name: FILE_HOST_PORT_FILE
variables.help: Where to record the port actually listened on, as `{ port, pid }`, for `paulgsc/some-ui`'s `vite dev` to find (`listen::PortFile`). Removed on shutdown. `make dev` sets it

variables.name: RATE_LIMIT
variables.help: Rate limit, in requests per minute, per client (`main.rs`'s `rate_limit_middleware` partitions by peer IP). See #215/#231: this field previously declared the right unit but was unread — the limiter's capacity was `max_request_size` (megabytes of upload payload) instead

variables.name: ALLOWED_ORIGINS
variables.help:
Comma-separated list of allowed CORS origins for browser-facing read routes (push and sessions). Other routes deliberately allow any origin (extensions, etc.) and are unaffected by this setting.

Required: no list is right on every host (#406). Include the HTTPS origin the study app is served from, not only Storybook's `:6006`: service workers, `Notification`, and `PushManager` are all gated on a secure context, so a subscription is posted from an HTTPS origin. The dev host sets `https://nixos.local:5173,https://localhost:5173,http://nixos.local:6006`.

variables.name: REDIS_URL
variables.help:
Redis URL for caching.

Unset, a Redis on this machine (HOST-SPECIFIC; see `DEV_HOST_REDIS_URL`).

variables.name: CACHE_TTL
variables.help: Cache TTL in seconds

variables.name: MAX_REQUEST_SIZE_MB
variables.help: Individual request payload lmit in MB

variables.name: MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS
variables.help: Active request limit

variables.name: TASK_TIMEOUT_MS
variables.help: Hard timeout for any operation

variables.name: DATABASE_URL
variables.help:
The `SQLite` database, as `sqlite://<path>`.

The container sets its own (`infra/compose/file_host.yml`), and `make dev` its own, `deploy/dev/file_host.env`'s. Pointed at the directory the container mounts, a dev run opens the container's live database.

variables.name: NUDGE_ENABLED
variables.help:
Whether the daily nudge tick runs at all.

With this off, the `/push` routes still work — a browser can subscribe and a manual send can be triggered — but nothing fires on a schedule. On, the server refuses to start without a usable VAPID pair. A dev run beside the container keeps it off, or a learner is nudged twice.

variables.name: VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY
variables.help:
VAPID public key, base64url, uncompressed P-256 point.

Handed to the browser as `applicationServerKey`. It is baked into every subscription made with it, so changing it does not re-key them — it silently invalidates all of them. Treat rotation as a migration. Generate a pair with `npx web-push generate-vapid-keys`.

variables.name: VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY
variables.help: VAPID private key, base64url, the raw 32-byte P-256 scalar. Secret

variables.name: VAPID_SUBJECT
variables.help: The VAPID `sub` claim: a `mailto:` or an origin URL identifying the sender. Push services reject or deprioritise senders without one

variables.name: NUDGE_TIMEZONE
variables.help:
IANA timezone name deciding when a day starts and when quiet hours apply.

Deliberately an `Option` with no default. A container is UTC unless told otherwise, and a silent UTC fallback is how an evening reminder arrives at 3am; leaving this unset is allowed but is logged as the choice it is. A name that is not an IANA zone (`America/Denvr`) stops the server at start (#407); it used to fall back to UTC.

variables.name: NUDGE_QUIET_HOURS_START
variables.help: Local hour, 0-23, at which nudges stop

variables.name: NUDGE_QUIET_HOURS_END
variables.help: Local hour, 0-23, at which nudges resume. May be less than the start hour; the range wraps midnight. Equal bounds mean no quiet hours at all

variables.name: NUDGE_WAKER_SECONDS
variables.help:
How often the waker picks up work the engine already decided.

Not a schedule. Eligibility instants are solved when signals arrive and written to an index; this is the resolution at which they are noticed, so shortening it lands interventions closer to their computed instant without changing which ones happen.

variables.name: PUSH_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT_MS
variables.help:
How long one push delivery may take before it counts as a failure (#264, SLI3).

A push service that accepts answers in well under a second; one that has not answered in ten is not going to, and every second past that is a second the rest of the batch waits in the serial loop. Long enough that a slow-but-working provider on a bad day is not misread as down, short enough that one black-holed endpoint costs a pass seconds rather than the transport's own (unbounded) patience. A timed-out delivery is recorded as a failure — never a prune, never `Accepted` — and does not hand the claim back: see `nudge::waker::actuate`.

variables.name: WAKER_PASS_DEADLINE_MS
variables.help:
How long one waker pass may run before it stops taking on new subjects (#264, SLI3).

Two minutes: well inside `NUDGE_WAKER_SECONDS`' default of five, so a pass that hits it still leaves the next tick to start on time rather than be delayed by `MissedTickBehavior::Delay`, and long enough for a full `BATCH` of 32 subjects at typical sub-second delivery latency to finish many times over. A pass that runs out starts no further subject and tries no further device — each delivery's timeout is also capped at what the pass has left — but never cancels a subject part-way, so a claim already written stands. Subjects it did not reach are still due on the next pass, the property `BATCH` already relies on.

variables.name: RECOMMENDER_USES_OUTCOMES
variables.help: Whether the recommender ranks a provisioned session with this subject's outcome history (#289, TEL4). **Off by default, and meant to stay off until someone has looked at real data** — see `docs/study-nudge.md`, "Outcome stats and the flag that gates them", for what would justify turning it on. Off, the recommender sees every activity as unplayed, exactly as it did before `activity_outcome` existed

variables.name: NUDGE_PRESENCE_LEASE_TTL_SECONDS
variables.help:
How long a client-written presence lease stays fresh before a due subject's notification is sent as though nobody were looking.

Renamed from `NUDGE_PRESENCE_FRESHNESS_SECONDS` (default `120`) when presence stopped being a WebSocket connection's staleness window and became a lease TTL: same shape of question, a different mechanism underneath, and a smaller default — a client renewing roughly every 45s while visible only needs a TTL wide enough to absorb timer throttling and scheduling jitter, not two minutes of slack.

variables.name: APP_BASE_URL
variables.help:
Base URL of the study app, used to build the notification's deep link. Must end with a slash: the client builds `${BASE_URL}sessions/${id}` and the server has to produce the same shape or clicks land on the dashboard.

Required: no URL is right on every host (#406). The dev host sets `https://nixos.local:5173/`.

variables.name: AUTH_ENABLED
variables.help:
Whether passkey sign-in is on.

On by default. On, `WEBAUTHN_RP_ID` and `WEBAUTHN_ORIGINS` are required and the server will not start without them. `false` is for a run that needs nobody signed in: every ceremony answers `503` and every subject-scoped route `401`. `false` with `WEBAUTHN_RP_ID` set is refused as a contradiction.

variables.name: WEBAUTHN_RP_ID
variables.help: The WebAuthn relying party id: the registrable domain the app is served from (`nixos.local`, `example.com`), with no scheme or port. A passkey is bound to it for good, so changing it strands every passkey made under the old one, which also makes it HOST-SPECIFIC in the strongest sense: moving to a new domain strands every passkey made on this one. Required while `AUTH_ENABLED` is on. For local development on `https://localhost:5173`, `localhost`

variables.name: WEBAUTHN_ORIGINS
variables.help: Comma-separated origins the app is served from, scheme and port included (`https://nixos.local:5173`). A passkey ceremony from any other origin fails verification. Required when `WEBAUTHN_RP_ID` is set

variables.name: AUTH_SESSION_DAYS
variables.help: How long a sign-in lasts, in days. It slides: opening the app past the halfway point renews it to a full term

variables.name: AUTH_OPEN_SIGNUP
variables.help: Whether an account may be created while one already exists. Off (the default), the first account closes sign-up: the box is one person's, and that account is the owner's, which runs the operator routes and is whose copy the Jobs mailbox is kept as, with no subject id set anywhere here. On, for a product where anyone who can reach the server may make an account; then no account is the owner's by itself, and `OPERATOR_SUBJECTS` and `MAILBOX_SUBJECT` say who is who. Sign-in is open either way

variables.name: AUTH_NEW_ACCOUNTS_PER_DAY
variables.help: How many accounts may be created per UTC day, across the server, with `AUTH_OPEN_SIGNUP` on. A backstop against a flood of empty accounts; the per-client rate limit already bounds any one client

variables.name: OPERATOR_SUBJECTS
variables.help:
Comma-separated subject ids allowed to use the operator routes: the ones that rewrite, retire and restore what everyone is served (lessons, `leetype` rounds). Whitespace around an entry is trimmed and empty entries are ignored. Unset or empty, the owner's account (the only one) is the operator, and nobody is while the box has no account or several. Set, only the listed subjects are: an override for a deployment with `AUTH_OPEN_SIGNUP` on; see `auth::operator`.

To find a subject id to list, sign in where you operate from and call any operator route: the refusal is logged at info with your `subject=`.

variables.name: MAILBOX_ENABLED
variables.help: Whether home reads the Jobs mailbox at all. On, the server refuses to start unless `MAILBOX_URL` and `MAILBOX_TOKEN` are set and usable

variables.name: MAILBOX_URL
variables.help: The mailbox's base URL: `https://` and a host, no path (`https://some-ui-mailbox.<account>.workers.dev`)

variables.name: MAILBOX_TOKEN
variables.help: Home's own mailbox token: it reads `brief` and puts `decisions` and `scout`. Never logged

variables.name: MAILBOX_SUBJECT
variables.help: The subject whose copy the mailbox's files are kept as. Unset, the owner's account (the only one), read at each pass; while the box has no account or several, a pass keeps nothing and says `no_account`. Set, that subject: an override for a deployment with `AUTH_OPEN_SIGNUP` on, its id found as for `OPERATOR_SUBJECTS`

variables.name: MAILBOX_SECONDS
variables.help: Seconds between reads of the mailbox. At least 60

variables.name: ROUTINE_SCHEDULE
variables.help: When each routine that leaves run records in the mailbox is due: `<routine> <HH:MM> <IANA zone>` entries separated by `;`, the routine `jobs` or `reflections`. Empty expects no run. Read only with the mailbox on (`routine_watch`)

variables.name: MAILBOX_ARCHIVE_TOKEN
variables.help: Home's second mailbox token (the Worker's `ARCHIVE_TOKEN`): it moves a file live there long enough home, and puts one back when the routine asks. Unset, nothing is archived. Never logged

variables.name: MAILBOX_ARCHIVE_DAYS
variables.help: Days a file stays live in the mailbox before home archives it. At least 30, the mailbox's own floor

variables.name: FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_FILE
variables.help: A Google service account's JSON key, allowed to send through FCM for the app's Firebase project, as the container sees it: the repo's `config/` is mounted at `/app/config`, and a name with `secret` in it stays out of git (`.gitignore`'s `*secret*`), e.g. `/app/config/fcm-service-account-secret.json`. Unset, home tells no phone anything; set to a file that is not such a key, the server refuses to start

variables.name: TRANSCRIBE_ENABLED
variables.help: Whether home transcribes voice notes at all. On, the server refuses to start unless both models load and ffmpeg runs. Get the models with `nix develop .#whisper -c whisper fetch`

variables.name: TRANSCRIBE_MODEL
variables.help: The multilingual whisper.cpp model, as a path inside the container. The default is where `infra/compose/file_host.yml` mounts the host's models directory (HOST-SPECIFIC there), with the model `nix/whisper-manager` downloads

variables.name: TRANSCRIBE_VAD_MODEL
variables.help: The Silero VAD model that finds a note's speech, mounted beside it

variables.name: TRANSCRIBE_THREADS
variables.help: Threads one note is heard with. Unset, one fewer than the cores the container may use, and at least one

variables.name: TRANSCRIBE_DEADLINE_SECONDS
variables.help: Seconds one note may take, decoding included. At least 60

variables.name: TRANSCRIBE_SECONDS
variables.help: Seconds between looks for notes to hear. At least 10

variables.name: RUST_ROUNDS_ENABLED
variables.help: Whether home records Rust Rounds' programs. On, the rust-runner's socket must be mounted at `RUST_ROUNDS_SOCKET`; a runner that is not there is reported each pass, and nothing is recorded until it is

variables.name: RUST_ROUNDS_SOCKET
variables.help: The rust-runner's socket, as a path inside the container: where `infra/compose/rust_runner.yml`'s socket volume is mounted

variables.name: RUST_ROUNDS_SECONDS
variables.help: Seconds between looks for programs to record. At least 10

variables.name: RUST_ROUNDS_PASS_DEADLINE_SECONDS
variables.help: Seconds one pass may take, every program it records included. At least 142: the toolchain ask's wait and one program's, which outlasts the runner's job deadline

variables.name: GAME_FEED_ENABLED
variables.help: Whether home follows the games of the week at all

variables.name: GAME_FEED_SCOREBOARD_SECONDS
variables.help: Seconds between reads of the week's scoreboard. At least 60

variables.name: GAME_FEED_LIVE_SECONDS
variables.help: Seconds between reads of a live game's play-by-play. At least 5

variables.name: GAME_FEED_BACKOFF_CAP_SECONDS
variables.help: The longest a refused or failed fetch waits before the next try. At least both cadences above, and at most 86400 (a day)

variables.name: NATS_URL
variables.help:
The NATS server to connect to.

The default only works beside a NATS that publishes 4222 on the same machine (a `cargo run` next to the compose stack). HOST-SPECIFIC: see `some_transport::DEV_HOST_NATS_URL`. Every container sets it.

variables.name: RUST_LOG
variables.help:
`tracing` filter directives, e.g. `info,async_nats=warn`.

A filter that does not parse stops the binary at start.

variables.name: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
variables.help: The OTLP (gRPC) collector traces are exported to, e.g. `http://otel-collector:4317`. Unset, they are not exported at all: nothing in the compose stack runs a collector, and metrics go through Prometheus (#139, #407)

variables.name: OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER
variables.help: Which traces are kept: all (`always_on`), none (`always_off`), or the share `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG` names (`traceidratio`)

variables.name: OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG
variables.help: With `traceidratio`, the share of traces kept, from 0 to 1

variables.name: ENVIRONMENT
variables.help: The `service.environment` traces carry

variables.name: OTEL_SERVICE_NAME
variables.help: The `service.name` traces are exported under. Leave it unset: it defaults to the binary's own name, and a value in a `.env` that more than one binary loads renames all of their traces
